question: Why did the first alpha-edge run report byte-identical DoF-on and DoF-off pairs?
answer: The renderer was not inert. The probe generator flipped only camera.dof.enabled; the frozen plan also carries 1350 camera_samples, and the runtime evaluates Camera2_5D from the samples, so every sample still had dof.enabled=true. Both 'off' probes were DoF-on renders.

before_fix.observed_symptom: A (probe-dof-off-030) and C (probe-dof-on-030) were both SHA-256 56cb69b16049875023149b62dc1758c0718328727e06d8cb165f5efffbbd1a8f

code_path: src/render_plan/render_plan_compiler_animation_utils.cpp: make_camera_evaluator() uses plan.camera_samples when present; a top-level-only edit cannot change the evaluated camera
src/render_plan/render_plan_compiler_scene_setup.cpp: the camera_evaluator result is installed as the scene camera
src/render_graph/pipeline/scene_context_setup.cpp: the scene camera is published to frame_input.camera_2_5d and has_camera_2_5d
src/render_graph/nodes/composite_node.cpp: the native layer DoF gate reads frame_input.camera_2_5d.dof.enabled
src/render_graph/nodes/composite_dof_provenance.cpp: dof_source_radius() computes a non-zero radius; the software run logged radius=28.00 while the old 'off' probe still had sample DoF enabled
diagnostic_log_that_settled_it: software render of probe-dof-off (before the generator fix) logged [dof-provenance] switching to mixed residency ... depth=2000.00 radius=28.00, proving the DoF was active despite camera.dof.enabled=false
conclusion: No renderer change was needed. make_probe_plans.py now writes the DoF switch to camera and every camera_sample; the unchanged frozen contract yields aggregate PASS with zero Vulkan validation errors.
